disclaimer: These figures are dated manual snapshots from free public reports. War-risk percentages are news-reported ranges, not a quote and not a market index. They vary by vessel, flag, cargo, itinerary and no-claims terms, and they can move quickly. The Joint War Committee does not set premiums. Not insurance advice.

war_risk_ap.title: War-risk additional premiums (news-reported, not a quote)

rows.area: Strait of Hormuz / Middle East Gulf (hull war, tankers)
rows.range: 7–9%, some cover written as low as 5%

rows.note: 9 Nov 2026. Rates have eased despite 110+ claims (about US$2.5bn); some Hormuz no-claims bonuses return up to half the premium, so headline rates overstate what owners pay.

iumi.title: IUMI marine insurance statistics (2025 year, published 2026)
iumi.source: IUMI Stats Report 2026 and accompanying press releases
points: Global marine insurance premiums USD 42.6 billion in 2025, up 5.5% on 2024.
Ocean hull USD 10.5 billion, up 9.4% (fleet growth, higher values and war premiums contributed).
Europe ocean-hull loss ratio about 60% on an incurred basis, including IBNR. Asia and the US about 50% on a paid-claims basis — the bases are not directly comparable.

allianz.title: Allianz Safety and Shipping Review 2026
allianz.source: Allianz Commercial, Safety and Shipping Review 2026
points: 43 total losses in 2025 (more than 30 of those ships over 500 GT).
2,818 reported incidents on vessels over 100 GT in 2025, down about 16% from 3,353 in 2024.
Machinery damage or failure was the main cause, at 1,505 incidents.
Over 200 fire incidents in 2025, the second-highest total in 10 years.
350 total losses in 2021–2025, an average of 70 a year, 37% lower than the 555 losses in 2016–2020.

emsa.title: EMSA Annual Overview of Marine Casualties and Incidents 2026
emsa.source: European Maritime Safety Agency, covering EU Member States, Iceland and Norway (EMCIP)
points: 2,630 marine casualties and incidents recorded in 2025, about 2% below the ten-year annual average.
52 very serious casualties; 29 fatalities (the lowest annual figure in 2016–2025); 813 injuries; 16 ships lost.
26,802 occurrences were recorded over 2016–2025 as a whole.
